deichman.description:
Photo of the interior of Deichman Bjørvika, the main library of Oslo Public Library (Deichman) located between the Central Station and the Oslo Opera House in Oslo, Norway. Deichman Bjørvika opened in June 2020 and spans 18,000 square meters across six floors, housing 450,000 books.
  • Basement – Bookshelves in the archive/magazine; Cinema; Auditorium for 150 people
  • 1st floor – Entrances; Coffee bar/restaurant; Reception area; Information desk, lending machines, retrieval shelves; shop; Lars Ramberg's 'Brainstorm' light installation, comprising 400 meters of neon tubes
  • 2nd floor – Fiction books for adults and children; Newspaper and magazine corner on the mezzanine; Café with access to a rooftop terrace
  • 3rd floor – Music, films, comics, games, and fantasy literature; Options for hobby activities ("People's Workshop" with printers, etc.); Podcast studio; DJ stations; Mini cinema; Game room; Small stage
  • 4th floor – Books on art, architecture, health, technology, and natural sciences; Classroom; Group rooms; Study spaces
  • 5th floor – Books on social sciences, history, psychology, philosophy, and religion; Study spaces.
In the cantilever between the fourth and fifth floors, there is a larger open section that extends 18 meters over the public square below, offering reading spaces and panoramic views of the city, overlooking the eastern part of Oslo harbour, the Akershus Fortress, and the Oslo Fjord.
  • In competition with 31 other libraries, Deichman Bjørvika was named "Public Library of the Year" in 2021 by the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions (IFLA):
Since June 2020, the library's spectacular glass façade has been reflecting in Oslo Harbour. In the basement, you'll find a cinema, an auditorium, a bar... and hundreds of thousands of books in the archive. On the first floor, there is a mezzanine with a newspaper corner, a restaurant, a café, an information desk, and book lending vending machines. Above that, there is a world of music, films, comics, and games, with digital equipment, a stage, and studios. For those seeking tranquility, a study place, or a panoramic view of the city, you can go up to the last two floors. There's even a classroom.
Photo taken by the librarian and "libro tourist" Charlotte Henard in July 2023. The image is part of a Flickr album showing the rooms, furnishings, fixtures and people inside the concrete building behind the glass facades, including doors, windows, stairs, excalators, railings, plant wall, furniture, shelves, chairs, tables, seating, books, loan machines, computers and equipment, signage, art, visitors, borrowers, librarians and staff, and more.

epicenter.credit:
Internet Archive identifier: capacitybuilding109455095
https://archive.org/download/capacitybuilding109455095/capacitybuilding109455095.pdf
epicenter.description:
The Horn of Africa has become an epicenter of interest for the global community due to the drastic increase in piracy. Indicative of the Gulf of Aden's strategic importance is the fact that more than 30,000 ships per year and 3 million barrels of oil per day transit the Suez Canal. Indicative of the severity of the problem of piracy is the fact that more than 30 countries are committing naval forces as part of a solution to the problem. The international community seeks to secure the area and protect the global economy. This thesis attempts to provide an innovative sustainable capacity building conceptual model to tackle piracy through the employment of cutting edge technological assets, i.e tethered aerostat radar sensors, UAVs and picosatellites. The economic and technical feasibility of the proposed conceptual model is tackled respectively by illustrating a scenario and providing an economic cost benefit approach regarding the cost of the proposed infrastructure. The conceptual model consists of a complex set of various components that, together, build an integrated architectural set constituting an innovative, alternative capacity-building model aiming to secure maritime traffic corridors, and at the same reducing the economic cost significantly and the number of deployed naval assets.


Subjects: Piracy
epicenter.title: File:Capacity building as an answer to piracy in the Horn of Africa (IA capacitybuilding109455095).pdf

epicenter.credit:
Internet Archive identifier: financingnavalsu109455623
https://archive.org/download/financingnavalsu109455623/financingnavalsu109455623.pdf
epicenter.description:
The United States Defense (DoD) does not budget for contingencies. The DoD does not set aside funds in the expectation of war, disaster, or other unexpected catastrophe, where obligation of those funds is contingent on the event actually occurring. This includes budgeting ahead for possible humanitarian assistance and disaster response (HA/DR) operations. Stability operations are now a core U.S. military mission, and humanitarian assistance and disaster response is one of six expanded core capabilities for the Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard enumerated in A Cooperative Strategy for 21st Century Seapower. This represents a monumental strategic shift for an establishment traditionally defined by hard power assets. This thesis uses a disaster categorization method based on size of the area affected and speed of disaster onset, and employs a multiple, flexible design case study method that analyzes incremental cost data from the responses to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, the 2010 Haiti earthquake and the 2010 Pakistan floods. Costs are analyzed for both their timing and the associated functional service provided, and are presented in graphical format. Despite the variety of HA/DR operations and the common belief that every disaster is different, this research identifies similarities in cost timing and function that exist across three of the four types of disaster. These findings provide insight into expected future demand, and highlight the functions that represent the greatest leverage points for future optimization.


Subjects: Disaster relief; Humanitarian assistance; Controllership
epicenter.title: File:Financing naval support for humanitarian assistance and disaster response an analysis of cost drivers and cash flows (IA financingnavalsu109455623).pdf

munch.description:
Photo taken from the Langkaia pier in Bjørvika, Oslo, towards the Ekeberg hill along which the historical town, spelled variously as Oplso, Anslo or Oslo in historical sources, once were located (a huge fire in 1624 prompted the king to move the town across the bay to Akersneset and rename it after himself, Christiania, a name it kept until taking its old name back in 1925).
The gray apartments buildings along the waterfront are part of the new Sørenga development while the tall building to the left, known as Lambda, will house the new Munch museum which is scheduled to open up in the autumn 2020.

uio.description:
Høsttakkefest Universitetsplassen (Original bildetekst)



Omtalt i hovedoppslaget på første side i Aftenposten mandag 7. oktober 1940:

Det nye Europa under Tysklands og Italias ledelse. Eneste oppgave – arbeide for sine folks vel, og å tjene dem i ro, fred og orden. Tale av Reichskommissar Terboven ved den tyske høsttakkefest igår.

Den tyske høsttakkefest på Universitetsplassen igår hadde samlet tusener av mennesker, som overvar høitideligheten. Midt på plassen var det reist en mektig «høststang» med et stort opbygget podium omkring. På universitetsbygningene var fasadene pyntet med mange flagg og på universitetstrappens nederste avsats var det reist en talerstol, smykket med store rognebærklaser og granbar og flankert av kornnek. Ved siden av talerstolen bugnet det på to border av markens grøde, store gresskar, gulerotbunter og blomkål, vindrueklaser og annen frukt. Rundt omkring var plassert bondens viktigste redskaper under optagningen, hakker, spader og grep.

På universitetstrappen var det plass for innbudte, tilvenstre på plassen var en del av arbeidstjenesten oppstillet og bak denne et musikkorps, som allerede en halv time før den egentlige høsttakkefest begynte underholdt den stadige strøm av mennesker. Blandt æresgjestene merket man sig generaloberst von Falkenhorst og generaloberst Stumpf.

Presis klokken 13 kom Reichskommissar Terboven ledsaget av sitt følge og til fanfarer fra militærmusikk-korpset. Musikken spilte så et par nummer hvorefter Landesgruppenleiter for NSDAP Spanhaus overrakte høstkransen til der Reichskommissar med en kort tale. Arbeidstjenesten sang derefter «Unsere Spaten im Frieden» og så kom ballletten fra Hamburger Staaatsoper, som på det opbyggede podium under høstkransen danset en vakker kostymedans i lyse, lette drakter med sorte kyser med lange sorte silkebånd. De høstet sterk applaus for sin grasiøse dans.

Et blandet kor fra Hamburger staatsoper fikk så sterkt bifall for sine sanger «Mein Mädel hat einen Rosenmund» og «Der Lidenbaum». Efter et musikkstykke sang arbeidstjenesten «Gott segne die Arbeit!», hvorefter balletten, denne gang forsterket med fire herrer, høstet livlig bifall for et nytt nummer.

Der Reichskommissar Terboven besteg så talerstolen og takekt for overleveringen av høtkransen. Der reichskommissar uttalte videre:(...)

Nasjonal Samling, forkortet NS, var et norsk politisk parti som ble grunnlagt av Vidkun Quisling i 1933 og ble oppløst ved frigjøringa i 1945. Ideologisk fulgte partiet den tyske nasjonalsosialismen, og NS ble støtteorganisasjon for den tyske okkupasjonsmakta i Norge under andre verdenskrig.
